english_verification.review_scope: Translated all source Markdown before the National Ideas appendix and all 41 non-national-ideas input pointers. Read representative current-Mod passages and three actual English Wiki chunks; this is not an exhaustive mission-tree or lore audit. The primary compared native idea names/descriptions with current English localisation keys (formatting codes stripped); B32 upgraded Farranean originals also use their separate flavour file. Wide source bounds are locator envelopes, not exhaustive line-by-line audits. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The Kingdom of Rogieria Wiki page is mostly an infobox and short notes, not a detailed history. Its 1553 and 1582 notes are setting chronology, not guaranteed campaign outcomes.
The Rogier the Exiled Wiki chronology (including 1447 and 1473) is fixed setting lore and does not determine the player's formation date.
No exhaustive review of every mission reward or all current Mod narrative text was performed.

rationale.campaign_length: The current local script contains 66 direct B37 missions, with the later campaign reaching old Dameria and the imperial throne.
rationale.colonization: The campaign begins with an Escanni adventurer company settling; overseas colonization is not its late-game focus.
rationale.complexity: You must coordinate adventurer formation, urban reconstruction, three legacy scores, diplomatic intrigue, and war.
rationale.dark_story: Dynastic collapse, revenge, secret politics, and an autocratic path make parts of the story grim, but inclusion and reconstruction are also prominent.
rationale.difficulty: Early regional competition is intense; later missions span Escann and the Empire, with substantial financial pressure.
rationale.diplomacy: Family ties, the crown, the Shadowmoon Conspiracy, and aligning imperial princes are central.
rationale.early_pressure: B07 first competes for land in post-Greentide Escann; forming B37 still requires technology and settlement conditions.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Family lore and faith are distinctive, but there is no comparably central spellcasting or artificery loop.
rationale.narrative_density: The exile, Young Owl, three legacies, ancestral remembrance, and conspiracy to return home form a continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: Developing Taranton, Balmire, and the northern frontier is important, but this is not a purely tall campaign.
rationale.trade_economy: Rebuilding towns, tea, and workshops sustain the state, but the economy serves political and military goals.
rationale.warfare: Taking land in Escann, defending the frontier, and returning to the Empire all require military strength.

identity.appearance: Starts in 1444 as the B07 Sons of Dameria adventurer company; after settling, it forms B37 and switches to its dedicated missions.

predecessors.relationship: The 1444 starting adventurer company; forming B37 changes the Tag and missions.

successors.relationship: An optional detour after meeting generic formation requirements; it changes the Tag and mission tree.

gaps.reason: No unambiguous tag/culture national idea definition found; no predecessor inference.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
At the end of the Lilac Wars in 1443 one of the last remaining Silmunas, Rogier Silmuna, son of Adenn Skylance and rightful heir to the Grand Duchy of Dameria and the Empire of Anbennar, had no choice but to flee his homeland and seek shelter amongst the marcher lords that made their way to Escann to fight the Greentide.

The heirs of Rogieria share blood with Rogier, and claim themselves as the last true Silmunas in Anbennar, as their Wesdamerian cousins had fought against Dameria in the war.

description.text:
The Sons of Dameria were composed of exiled soldiers and nobility that once served under Grand Duchy of Dameria. Resigned to their fate as losers of the war, many sought a new life of valour elsewhere in fighting the Greentide.

By the 1800s these men and women who lost everything and proceeded to fight for a place that held no stake to them was one of the main catalysts for the Romantic movement.

description.text: Despite their self-imposed exile, many important members of Rogieria still hold family ties to those remaining in Anbennar and the rest of Cannor. Ties that can be called upon for Rogieria's gain.

description.text: Many years after Rogier's death a man named Owen the Mad began to rave about how Rogier was one of the most important and best Silmunas around. This eventually spread across Rogieria and reinforced the idea of Silmuna hegemony and the quasi-worship of Rogier within Rogierian beliefs and traditions, much to the dismay of its neighbours.

description.text:
"Reclaim What Is Ours"
-House Words of the Rogierian Silmunas

Long scorned from their homeland, the King Ellís of Rogieria eventually made peace with the Wesdamerian branch of the family and joined houses with his marriage with Duchess Laurentíne. Years later he infamously tried to reclaim the Grand Duchy of Dameria and lost Wesdam's lands in Madelaire - after that his son Lothane II fought for much of his short life to defend his territories but eventually lost both Wesdam and Rogieria by 1582.

description.text: Named after the Rogierian flag which contains the elven moon on black, the Shadowmoon Conspiracy is allegedly a hidden network of Silmuna loyalists that plot to put a Silmuna back on the imperial throne of Anbennar.

description.text: The Silmunas have sat on the imperial throne of Anbennar for much of its history, and by the graces of the gods an Anbennar without a Silmuna is no Anbennar at all.

description.text: Dameria's position as lord of the Damesear has allowed it to become a great power across all of Cannor, but to protect the isle from any would-be invaders it must be protected by a wooden wall: the finest ships in the Dameshead.

description.text: Before the Grand Duchy was the Kingdom, and before the Kingdom was the Republic: the ancient force that civilized all of Cannor and made it what it is today.

description.text: At the highest hill of Anbenncóst sits the Imperial Palace, formerly the Damerian Palace. Though no doubt, the strength of Dameria lies not in its diplomacy, nor its traditions, but the people of Anbenncóst that form the foundation of all things right.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid if you dislike high-pressure land-grabbing, prolonged urban development, and campaigns spanning both Escann and the Empire.
player_overview.how_it_plays: First seize land and settle in Escann; then expand and rebuild Rogieria while managing the family and half-orc politics; later reconnect with imperial holdovers and contest the throne.
player_overview.overview: Lead the Sons of Dameria in the struggle for land in post-Greentide Escann, then settle and establish Rogieria. The Young Owl and the family’s old retainers must rebuild towns, make a place for half-orcs, and shape the new kingdom through autocracy, popular affection, or restoration of the old order. Once secure, use diplomacy, the Shadowmoon Conspiracy, and war to return home and claim the throne of the Anbennar Empire.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy character-driven restoration, an Escanni adventurer company, dynastic politics, and diplomatic intrigue.
signature_features: After the adventurer company forms a kingdom, a long succession story follows the exiled family and the Young Owl.
Mission choices accumulate three Silmuna legacies that shape the kingdom’s political character and outcomes.
The Shadowmoon Conspiracy connects diplomacy, espionage, and war in the return to the Empire.
player_overview.tagline: Build a kingdom from Damerian exiles and lead the Silmuna family back toward the imperial throne.

reasons: A clear character succession carries the story from adventurer company to Silmuna kingdom.
The three legacies and the Young Owl give choices lasting consequences.
The Shadowmoon Conspiracy makes restoration more than a sequence of mindless declarations of war.
warnings: The predecessor B07 must first seize land in Escann and form B37.
Urban reconstruction and cross-region missions can create financial pressure.
Forming A58 Dameria changes the Tag and mission tree again; decide whether to leave B37 Rogieria’s main path.

values.rationale: Half-orcs are explicitly included in farming, scholarship, citizenship, and advisory roles, and the story offers clemency and a popular-ruler path. Dynastic restoration and the imperial claim primarily affect expansion and authoritarianism and should not be double-counted against values.
red_flags: Secret politics and a war of restoration
